title: Work & Meetings
description: Everyday English for the office: meetings, emails, deadlines, projects, careers and negotiations.

items.translation: уложиться в срок, успеть к сроку
items.definition: to finish a piece of work by the time it was supposed to be finished
items.example: The whole team stayed late to [meet the deadline] for the client report.
items.exampleRu: Вся команда задержалась на работе, чтобы успеть сдать отчёт клиенту в срок.
items.trap: Not 'fit into a deadline' (calque of «уложиться в срок»); you meet or miss a deadline.

items.definition: to arrange a time and place for a meeting
items.example: Could you [set up a meeting] with the marketing team for next Tuesday?
items.exampleRu: Можешь назначить встречу с отделом маркетинга на следующий вторник?
items.pattern: set up a meeting with sb (for + time)
items.trap: Not 'appoint a meeting' (calque of «назначить встречу»); you appoint people to jobs.

items.definition: to decide that a planned event will not happen
items.example: The CEO was ill, so they had to [call off] the annual conference.
items.exampleRu: Гендиректор заболел, поэтому ежегодную конференцию пришлось отменить.
items.pattern: call sth off / call off sth
items.trap: Call off = cancel completely; to move an event to a later date, use 'put off' or 'postpone'.

items.definition: to change the time or date of a planned event
items.example: Something urgent has come up — can we [reschedule] our call to Thursday?
items.exampleRu: Возникло срочное дело — можем перенести наш созвон на четверг?
items.trap: Not 'transfer the meeting' (calque of «перенести встречу»). 'Postpone' or 'put off' = only to a later time; 'reschedule' or 'move' = any new time.

items.definition: to be behind the planned time
items.example: Sorry, my previous call is [running late], so I'll join in ten minutes.
items.exampleRu: Извините, предыдущий созвон затянулся, я подключусь минут через десять.
items.trap: Usually in the continuous form: 'I'm running late', not 'I run late'.

items.definition: to agree or have the same understanding about something
items.example: Let's have a quick call so everyone is [on the same page] before the launch.
items.exampleRu: Давайте быстро созвонимся, чтобы перед запуском все одинаково понимали задачу.
collocations: get everyone on the same page
items.pattern: be on the same page (about sth)
items.trap: Not 'on one page'. Don't mix it up with 'on the same wavelength' («на одной волне» = think and feel alike).

items.definition: to take further action or check on something after an earlier contact
items.example: I'm writing to [follow up on] our conversation about the new contract.
items.exampleRu: Пишу, чтобы вернуться к нашему разговору о новом контракте.
items.pattern: follow up on sth / follow up with sb
items.trap: Verb is two words (follow up), noun and adjective take a hyphen (a follow-up).

items.definition: to reply to someone later, usually with information they asked for
items.example: Let me check the figures and I'll [get back to you] by the end of the day.
items.exampleRu: Дайте мне проверить цифры, и я отвечу вам до конца дня.
collocations: get back to sb on sth
get back to sb with an answer
items.trap: Not 'return to you' («вернусь к вам»); 'get back to you' is the natural phrase.

items.definition: to keep someone informed about what is happening
items.example: Please [keep me in the loop] if the client changes the requirements again.
items.exampleRu: Пожалуйста, держи меня в курсе, если клиент снова поменяет требования.
items.pattern: keep sb in the loop (about sth)
items.trap: Not 'keep me in the course' (calque of «держать в курсе»).

items.definition: to write the official notes of what is said and decided at a meeting
items.example: Anna usually [takes the minutes] at our weekly management meeting.
items.exampleRu: На наших еженедельных совещаниях руководства протокол обычно ведёт Анна.
items.trap: Not 'write a protocol': in English 'protocol' means rules of behaviour, the notes are 'minutes'.

items.definition: included in the list of things to be discussed at a meeting
items.example: The new hiring policy is the first item [on the agenda] this morning.
items.exampleRu: Новая политика найма стоит первым пунктом в сегодняшней утренней повестке.
items.trap: Use 'on' the agenda, not 'in' the agenda; 'agenda' is not a diary or planner.

items.definition: to go to a meeting and be present at it
items.example: I'm afraid I won't be able to [attend the meeting] on Friday — I'll be at a client's office.
items.exampleRu: К сожалению, я не смогу присутствовать на совещании в пятницу — буду у клиента.
items.trap: No preposition: 'attend a meeting', not 'attend at/on a meeting'. Not 'visit a meeting' (calque of «посетить»).

items.definition: to finish a meeting, task or discussion
items.example: We're almost out of time, so let's [wrap up] with a quick summary.
items.exampleRu: Время почти вышло, так что давайте закругляться и коротко подведём итоги.
items.pattern: wrap sth up / wrap up (with sth)

items.definition: to look at or discuss something carefully, often again
items.example: Can we [go over] the slides together before the presentation tomorrow?
items.exampleRu: Можем вместе пройтись по слайдам перед завтрашней презентацией?
items.trap: The object comes after 'over': 'go over the plan', not 'go the plan over'.

items.translation: дать обратную связь, высказать мнение (о работе)
items.definition: to tell someone what was good or bad about their work so that they can improve it
items.example: Could you [give me some feedback] on my first draft before Friday?
items.exampleRu: Можешь дать мне обратную связь по первому черновику до пятницы?
items.trap: Uncountable: not 'a feedback' or 'feedbacks'; say 'some feedback' or 'a piece of feedback'.

items.definition: to work more hours than your normal working time
items.example: During the busy season, most of the staff [work overtime] without complaining.
items.exampleRu: В горячий сезон большинство сотрудников без жалоб работают сверхурочно.
items.trap: 'Overtime' is one word and has no article here: not 'work an overtime'.

items.definition: to not go to work for one day, with permission
items.example: I'm going to [take a day off] on Friday to move into my new flat.
items.exampleRu: В пятницу я возьму выходной, чтобы переехать в новую квартиру.
items.trap: Not 'take a weekend' or 'take a day out' ('a day out' is a trip for fun).

items.definition: to be away from work because you are ill
items.example: Mark has [been on sick leave] since Monday, so I'm covering his clients.
items.exampleRu: Марк на больничном с понедельника, так что его клиентов веду я.
items.trap: Not 'on a hospital' (calque of «на больничном»); 'in hospital' means you are a patient there. Informally: 'be off sick'.

items.translation: подать заявку на вакансию, откликнуться на вакансию
items.definition: to formally ask to be considered for a job
items.example: She [applied for a job] at a tech startup after finishing her MBA.
items.exampleRu: После получения MBA она откликнулась на вакансию в технологическом стартапе.
items.pattern: apply for a job / apply to a company
items.trap: 'Apply for' a job or position, but 'apply to' a company or university.

items.definition: to be given a higher position at work
items.example: After two years in sales, he [got promoted] to regional manager.
items.exampleRu: Через два года работы в продажах его повысили до регионального менеджера.
items.trap: A promotion is a better job; more money is a 'pay rise' (US 'raise').

items.definition: to have your salary increased
items.example: I'm planning to ask my manager whether I can [get a pay rise] this year.
items.exampleRu: Я собираюсь спросить у начальника, можно ли мне в этом году получить прибавку.
items.trap: Not 'salary rising' or 'a rise of salary'; 'pay rise' is British, 'raise' is American.

items.translation: подать заявление об уходе, уволиться по собственному желанию
items.definition: to formally tell your employer that you are going to leave your job
items.example: After five years at the bank, she finally [handed in her notice] last week.
items.exampleRu: Проработав в банке пять лет, на прошлой неделе она наконец подала заявление об уходе.
items.trap: Not 'write a statement' (calque of «написать заявление»).

items.definition: to stop employing workers because there is not enough work or money
items.example: The factory [laid off] two hundred workers when orders dropped sharply.
items.exampleRu: Когда заказы резко упали, завод сократил двести рабочих.
items.pattern: lay sb off / be laid off
items.trap: 'Laid off' is because of cuts, not your fault; if it's for bad work, you are 'fired'. Past form is 'laid', not 'layed'.

items.definition: to move to higher and better jobs in your career
items.example: He spent his twenties trying to [climb the career ladder] at a big consulting firm.
items.exampleRu: Лет до тридцати он пытался подняться по карьерной лестнице в крупной консалтинговой компании.
items.trap: Not 'career stairs' (calque of «карьерная лестница»).

items.translation: баланс между работой и личной жизнью
items.definition: the right amount of time spent on work compared with free time and family
items.example: Working from home has really improved my [work-life balance] this year.
items.exampleRu: Удалёнка в этом году заметно улучшила баланс между моей работой и личной жизнью.
items.trap: Word order is fixed: 'work-life balance', not 'balance of work and life'.

items.definition: to have so much work that you can hardly deal with it
items.example: I'd love to help, but I'm [snowed under] with reports until Thursday.
items.exampleRu: Я бы с радостью помог, но до четверга я завален отчётами.

items.definition: to be the person who controls or is responsible for something
items.example: Olga is [in charge of] the whole onboarding process for new employees.
items.exampleRu: Ольга отвечает за весь процесс адаптации новых сотрудников.
collocations: put sb in charge of sth
items.pattern: be in charge of sth / doing sth
items.trap: Use 'of', not 'for': 'in charge of the budget', not 'in charge for the budget'.

items.translation: идти по плану, укладываться в график
items.definition: to be progressing as planned and likely to succeed
items.example: Despite a few delays, the project is still [on track] to launch in March.
items.exampleRu: Несмотря на некоторые задержки, проект по-прежнему идёт по плану и стартует в марте.
items.pattern: be on track to do sth / for sth

items.definition: to fail to do something as quickly as planned
items.example: We [fell behind] schedule because two developers left in the same month.
items.exampleRu: Мы отстали от графика, потому что в один месяц ушли сразу два разработчика.
items.pattern: fall behind (with sth) / fall behind schedule
items.trap: Not 'lag from the schedule' (calque of «отставать от графика»).

items.definition: at the latest possible time, just before something was supposed to happen
items.example: The client cancelled the meeting [at the last minute], after we'd prepared everything.
items.exampleRu: Клиент отменил встречу в последний момент, когда мы уже всё подготовили.
collocations: leave sth until the last minute
items.pattern: at the last minute / a last-minute + noun
items.trap: Not 'in the last moment' (calque of «в последний момент»); say 'at the last minute'.

items.definition: to accept that you are in charge of something or that it is your fault
items.example: The manager [took responsibility for] the mistake instead of blaming her team.
items.exampleRu: Руководитель взяла ответственность за ошибку на себя, а не стала обвинять команду.
items.pattern: take responsibility for sth / for doing sth
items.trap: Use 'for', not 'on': not 'take responsibility on yourself' (calque of «взять на себя»).

items.definition: to meet an employer who asks you questions to decide whether to give you a job
items.example: I [have a job interview] at a bank tomorrow, and I'm really nervous.
items.exampleRu: Завтра у меня собеседование в банке, и я очень нервничаю.
items.pattern: have a (job) interview with / at + company
items.trap: Not 'pass an interview' (calque of «пройти собеседование»): 'pass' means succeed. Say 'have / go for an interview'.

items.definition: to talk to a group of people about a subject, often using slides
items.example: I have to [give a presentation] to the board on our quarterly results.
items.exampleRu: Мне нужно выступить перед советом директоров с презентацией квартальных результатов.
items.pattern: give a presentation on/about sth (to sb)
items.trap: Not 'hold/conduct a presentation' (calques of «провести презентацию»).

items.definition: a formal phrase used in emails to say that a file is attached
items.example: [Please find attached] the updated budget for your review.
items.exampleRu: Во вложении — обновлённый бюджет на ваше рассмотрение.
items.trap: Not 'In the attachment you can find' (calque of «во вложении вы найдёте»).

items.definition: a common phrase in work emails meaning "as we talked about or agreed earlier"
items.example: [As discussed] on Monday, I've attached the revised contract.
items.exampleRu: Как мы и обсуждали в понедельник, прикладываю исправленный договор.
items.trap: 'Discuss' takes no preposition: 'as we discussed', 'discuss the contract', not 'discuss about the contract' (from «обсуждать / говорить о»).

items.definition: an informal way to say you will join a phone or video call
items.example: This is getting complicated; can we [jump on a call] for five minutes?
items.exampleRu: Всё становится запутанно, может, созвонимся минут на пять?
items.trap: Not 'call up with sb' («созвониться с кем-то»); say 'have a call with sb' or 'jump on a call'.

items.definition: to do your job at home instead of in an office
items.example: Most of our team [work from home] on Mondays and Fridays.
items.exampleRu: Большая часть нашей команды по понедельникам и пятницам работает из дома.
items.trap: Not 'I work on remote' (calque of «на удалёнке»); say 'I work from home' or 'I work remotely'.

items.definition: to agree to some of another person's demands so that you both can agree
items.example: They wanted a 20% discount, so we [met them halfway] and offered 10%.
items.exampleRu: Они хотели скидку 20 %, и мы пошли им навстречу, предложив 10 %.
items.trap: Not 'go towards sb' (calque of «пойти навстречу»).

items.definition: to reach an agreement, especially in business
items.example: After weeks of talks, the two companies finally [struck a deal] on Friday.
items.exampleRu: После нескольких недель переговоров компании наконец заключили сделку в пятницу.
items.pattern: strike a deal with sb (on sth)
items.trap: Not 'conclude a deal' in everyday speech; the past of strike is 'struck'.

items.definition: the most important fact in a situation; also a company's final profit or loss
items.example: [The bottom line] is that we can't afford to hire anyone this quarter.
items.exampleRu: Суть в том, что в этом квартале мы не можем позволить себе нанять кого-либо.
